result.summary: Introduces `util::ResultPtr`, a wrapper around `util::Result` designed for functions that return pointer types such as `std::unique_ptr`. It provides single-dereference syntax and ensures boolean conversions evaluate to false if the underlying pointer is null or if an error occurred, updating call sites in `LoadAddrman` and wallet loader interfaces.
result.problem: When `util::Result` wraps smart pointers, accessing the object requires awkward double-dereferencing (`**result` or `(*result)->member`). Furthermore, checking the result in a boolean context only verifies whether the operation succeeded, evaluating to true even when the returned pointer is null (#26004).
evidence: Partially addresses issue #26004 ('util::Result has confusing interface for std::*_ptr T').

PR description: 'Instead of needing to be deferenced twice with **result or (*result)->member, it only needs to be dereferenced once with *result or result->member. Also when it is used in a boolean context, instead of evaluating to true when there is no error and the pointer is null, it evaluates to false so it is straightforward to determine whether the result points to something.'
result.scope_notes: Stacked on top of #25665. Only the final two commits (`Add util::ResultPtr class` and `Use ResultPtr<unique_ptr> instead of Result<unique_ptr>`) are specific to this PR; the rest of the diff belongs to the base PR.
result.card: Introduces `util::ResultPtr`, a helper wrapper around `util::Result` for functions returning pointer types, and adopts it across `LoadAddrman` and wallet loader interfaces. It eliminates double-dereferencing (`**result`) and prevents bugs where boolean checks evaluate to true even when the contained pointer is null. This partially resolves issue #26004 regarding confusing pointer handling in `util::Result`. Depends on base PR #25665.
